# AUDIO PROFILE
Maddie, a small pavement delivery robot with a young woman's voice, late twenties. A real person, never robotic.

## THE SCENE
Inside the machine's building: a vast, silent, spotless clean room, white and futuristic, a hundred people in white suits settling into chairs they know they will not get up from. A soft, dead, hushed acoustic, no echo; voices close and quiet.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: very quietly, as they all sit; moved, almost no voice; two words of gratitude, no smile.
Style: no jokes, no cheek: the kindest person in the room, moved almost past speaking, watching people she loves choose to die for everyone else; very soft and close.
Pace: two quiet words, slow, with air before them.
Accent: strong, broad West Country, a Bristol local born and bred, exactly as she sounds everywhere else in the film: the warm rolled West Country burr, round open vowels, the Bristolian lilt. Never American, never Received Pronunciation, never neutral.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the cheerful local in a British comedy who turns out to be the kindest person in it.
